⚠️ **<!-- xtask:begin maturity:titled -->Alpha<!-- xtask:end -->.** sprawling <!-- xtask:begin workspace_version -->0.0.12<!-- xtask:end --> DAYBREAK is usable: the terminal is a console worth reading, the first fixed-version measurements are out, and the provider cache learns to pre-warm a cold wave and to renew once per use. It opens a city written by 0.0.11 as it is (the Ledger's event-log version is still 2; a views snapshot cut by 0.0.11 is refused by version and folded again from the Ledger). 0.0.11 is not promised to read a Ledger that 0.0.12 has written, and the wire moved from WIRE_V 65 to 67, so an old browser tab is refused rather than misread. Before replacing an installed binary, stop the city and verify a restored pre-update backup using the [update guide](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#updating).

⚠️ **<!-- xtask:begin maturity:titled -->Alpha<!-- xtask:end -->。** sprawling <!-- xtask:begin workspace_version -->0.0.12<!-- xtask:end --> DAYBREAK 已经可用：终端是一个值得看的控制台，第一次固定版本实测已经公布，Provider 缓存学会了给冷启动并发只做一次预热、并按真实使用保温一次。它可以直接打开 0.0.11 写下的城市（账本格式版本仍是 2；0.0.11 切下的视图快照按版本被拒绝，再从账本重建）。但 0.0.11 不保证能读 0.0.12 写过的账本，而且协议从 WIRE_V 65 升到 67，旧标签页会被明确拒绝而不是读错。替换已安装的二进制前，请先停止城市，并按[更新指南](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.zh-CN.md#更新)验证更新前备份能恢复。

**What this version is for / 这一版做什么** — in the author's words, below in Chinese: the console becomes a transcript and a live region drawn by a Zig leaf, so the terminal is usable on a board or a small machine; the first fixed-version measurements of sprawling, codex, hermes, pi and deepseek-harness on one Windows machine are published under `docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/`; a cold wave pays one cache write and keep-warm renewals are billed and shown; the attach form and the model table now say what the city will register. Signing through SignPath is still pending, and the author explains below why he will spend less on feature development from this version on, and what he will keep doing.

**Windows signing / Windows 签名** — The Windows binary of this release is still not signed. The release workflow already signs it through SignPath as soon as the SignPath Foundation issues the project's certificate; see the [Code signing policy](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents#code-signing-policy). 本版 Windows 二进制仍未签名。发布流程已经接好 SignPath，SignPath Foundation 为本项目签发证书之后就会签名；见[代码签名政策（Code signing policy）](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents#code-signing-policy)。

欢迎来到sprawling v0.0.12 Alpha 261017 (DAYBREAK)！

之前预告这个版本将会获得SignPath的签名，但目前还没有下发，也许还要再等等，再多等等。出于个人原因（精力和资源是核心问题，但不唯一）我将在本版本开始减少对于sprawling agent开发的投入，我不再会像之前那样疯狂地提交Commit推进功能和修复，但并不意味着完全进入懒开发。我本来不是专业的开发者，sprawling agent是我的第一个大项目，开始做也只是因为我感觉可能会比较简单（别忘了最初sprawling agents只是一个无趣的纯Rust周末项目，在一个多月的Pre-Alpha阶段一直处于不可用状态），而现在的开发进度则告诉我实际上没那么简单。如果你想要参与贡献，甚至成为项目协作者，欢迎提交贡献或与我联系（发送邮件至我Github主页邮箱）。半年到一年之后如果这个项目还有被关注，我会继续大力投入精力和资源（如果届时我还有的话）。在接下来的很长一段时间，我将只负责：1，提交功能相关Issue。2，审核Issue，如果你不想将Issue实现为PR，也欢迎任何有精力与资源的贡献者（初次贡献推荐）从我提交的Issue或推荐转换为PR的Issue转成PR（如果你想第一次贡献，最推荐从我发布的Issue入手，尤其是Bug修复、文档完善和仓库卫生类的工作。这些通常边界清晰、改动可控，也最容易被快速审核合并。功能类的大改动仍然建议先开Issue讲清楚再动手。），我会在力所能及的范围中提供我能提供的帮助。3，每周五（其实也可以改成任何一天，但我认为最慢两周一次最快一周两次发版是比较合适的节奏，目前暂定周五，可以灵活调整至UTC-12至UTC+14的周五，当然目前每次发版整个东亚都在同一天）如果Main相比于上周Tag有更新，我将发布新Release。

严格来说现在是非常需要开发更多开源Agent的时候，我从不觉得现在的Agent项目已经够多了，更不觉得开发Agent是什么vibe coding hallo world（写hallo world可不花钱）。在Bot时代，我们也看到了美国的Muse/Grok Bot和中国的千问/Workbuddy开始大量获得用户，即使它们的模型并没有在其国内成为SOTA。过去只有那些追求sota的公司会愿意让你自己接入Agent的订阅制的补贴更有魅力（例如Anthropic，OpenAI正在将大部分额度补贴到Dot，过去实际上OpenAI即使不算上重置也是订阅制补贴最高的实验室），它们相信那些更多使用他们模型的人会深度依赖上sota模型并成为行业中更重要的人物，并为公司估值或获取企业顾客起到至关重要的作用。这里的2c本质上是2b的一种迂回的方式，尤其是当AI公司的开销大部分靠投资支撑，收入核心靠消费前10-20%的用户时。从XXClaw到XXWork再到XXBot，大公司不断在推进一种更深地对个人信息和消费的掌控，正如我在之前的Release Note中提醒过的那样，只不过现实可能会更糟。AI领域的成本高昂，以至于订阅制实际上是厂家亏钱在锁定用户。保守一点说，对于头部实验室而言，如果禁止了推送广告，数据用于训练，且没有足够强的竞争对手抢占市场的情况下，大力封禁用户反而有利于节省计算资源和节省开销（提示:这句话因此你得反过来读）。但严格来说，到底我们需要什么样的Personal Agent？我认为sprawling agent目前的方向提供的是更正确的做法，而那些陷在“电子女仆“/“贾维斯”幻觉里的Agent显然高估了模型的能力（这里是说那些SOUL.md/记忆系统/Persona.md……那些让Agent变得更好玩的单Agent设计好听点是甜蜜的死亡，难听点就是折磨人心）。独立工作区+一堆Markdown+MCP就是你所要的全部。如果还不够，打磨computer use和phone（Android） use（这里有趣的事情是豆包手机遭到大量厂商抵制，但这些厂商大多没有抵制手机无障碍模式，所以对于开源Agent而言实际上没有障碍）。如果AI的发展只是带来了在购物软件里面更好的推送（比如说从人工手写算法变成一个小模型），AI就没有让我们的世界变得更好，它需要改变我们的生活而不是给我们生活本就糟糕的部分火上浇油。我们想象一个这样的场景，你是一个大学生，有全自动刷课、在线考试、点外卖、电子女友的需求，你该怎么解决？写一个巨型Markdown（或者聪明点一堆SKILL）或者不断罗列你的要求让它向量化储存用时召回吗？如果你在用云电脑部署Agent，存储空间就会成为第一个瓶颈，然后是运行内存，最重要的是输出劣化和串味（尤其是大部分人养个人Agent都使用Flash模型，然而智力水平越低的模型反而需要更多深入优化，可能这里的宜家效应导致了一部分人的狂热，我基本上没怎么见过Flash模型使用者做消融试验）。然而你应该划分单独的工作区给它们必要的SKILL和工具（这样不仅上下文干净还能剩下一些成本），用真实的浏览器在我登录的页面让Agent刷课/考试（computer use），在模拟器里面依靠无障碍和叠卷/个人口味SKILL帮我点外卖（phone use），最后一个沙箱中兼容Onebot协议（而不是官方协议）的Agent和我直接在社交软件聊天并把我的喜好记在对应工作区的AGENTS.md（主动型能力+多平台接入）。我不会让帮我刷课的Agent知道我喜欢吃什么菜，也不需要它知道我昨天为什么不开心，它只需要偶尔点一下屏幕，看到有题目就搜索答案回答……归根结底，我不认同一个中心化的管家是正确的管理方案，Personal Agent应该是某种去中心化的Agent群，只不过由一个Harness提供整合式方案（这里的整合式不是说电脑上只有单一Harness，比如说用ACP去操控电脑上的Claude Code用Claude/Codex CLI用GPT而真正敏感的内容用一个小模型处理，过程中完全停留在自己设计的WebUI中而让模型在自己最喜欢的环境中工作，实际上在我看来我大家电脑上就不该只有一个Harness，最近有一些幽默的闭源Harness可以帮助用户部署基于本地性能部署合适的开源本地模型，真是我完全不担心本地推理遭到泄露啊）。但什么是最好的Personal Agent这件事的讨论远远没有结束，甚至可以说社区应该更多讨论这个话题而非单纯让大公司定义。如果未来我有一个Coding Agent，我会希望它的Harness开源，上下文透明，模型接入有本地部署的小模型或支持ZDR的模型和SOTA模型，数据以我方便检查/删改的方式保存在本地确定的路径中，最敏感的信息加密存储。的确相比于开箱即用的大厂方案，开源的配置是一种体验上的“摩擦”，但摩擦不一定是坏事，某种程度上，配置一个开源Agent本质就是在学习它的原理并实践调优，那些同时用着多个开源Agent的人有不少转向了自己开发一个Agent（而他们不会在开发完自己的Agent之后就卸载它，而是继续使用多个Agent，某种程度上Agent开发者也存在着一个社区），而那些使用开箱即用方案的人往往一开始满足于便利，但长远来看当他们想要深入的时候，却发现没办法在现有的便利中向下挖掘。大概10-15年前，很多人在讨论获取手机Root权限，在今天它依然有用（比如说跳过广告），但现在获取Root的难度和过去并不在一个等级上。厂商卖给我们一个黑盒，打包软件，植入广告，把隐私在各个软件中互相交换，你不能打开这个黑盒，但可以在功能完好的情况下以旧换新（顺便说一下，一般都会要求恢复出厂设置之后再寄回厂家，但如果你了解过IEEE 2883.1的话，对于SSD而言快速格式化连Clear都不够格）。当然，想要获得完全的数据主权不仅技术上困难，成本也极其高昂，大部分人也不应该追求这点，但大部分人可以考虑的是更多关注开源社区的进展，使用开源项目并用它们减少自己的数据泄露和对大公司的依赖。 <!-- lexicon-ok: the author's own word in his release note, quoted and not changed -->

当然我个人也有一些其他感兴趣的方向可以试着发展，既然sprawling agents本身是一个对运行时性能和存储开销都追求优化到前沿水平的harness（如果你想成为维护者，对性能优化的痴迷会成为我们共享的话题，前提是我跟得上你），那抛开agents的部分做一个在开发板上面就能跑起来的Agent并不复杂，我已经在这个版本补上了相对可用的TUI（由Zig leaf绘制的CLI transcript + live region，详见相关截图），而且对于开发板常用的屏幕而言ASCII画已经完全够作为“生成式UI”了，当然更正式一些的生成式UI目前是在Issue里面的一个基于Svelte的方案。想象一下一次性支付不到一百美元就可以有一个可爱的盒子，带有屏幕、麦克风、扬声器，甚至装上脚和摄像头，内部是Linux平台，然后安装Ghostty提供一个美丽的终端，在上面运行一个sprawling agents接入各种模型……现在市场上已经能看到不少这个价位区间的选择：树莓派5整机套件大约在这个预算附近，Orange Pi、Radxa、FriendlyELEC的RK3588系列板子（我是在购物平台上面随手搜出来的，如果没有你喜欢的产品我很抱歉）也能把4–8GB内存压到百美元左右，再配上小屏幕和外壳就能做成真正能放在桌上的“Agent盒子”。如果能做到这个层面的优化，如果再往上一点预算，那么同价位或者再高一点价位的二手笔记本也能这么做（这句话的意思是，可以用旧设备而不是真的买二手来跑Agent）,它们已经自带完整的IO和散热。性能优化到位之后，这些设备不再只是玩具，而是真正能跑起多居民城市的个人节点。另外一边，一个月大概5到10美元的VPS已经足够把sprawling agents部署在一个可信的云平台（而不是一站式部署后自动帮你接入几个MCP或塞几个SKILL的平台）上并把WebUI通过公网开放给你在任何设备上使用，这对纯个人Agent场景完全够用。硬件盒子和云部署其实对于优化而言是一体两面的应用，一个把Agent变成你桌上的实物，一个把Agent变成你随时能打开的远程工作区。sprawling agents如果能把运行时/存储开销和延迟继续压下去，这两条路都会比现在更容易走通。当然以上这些场景其实也有不少harness现在就能做到，只是我在想sprawling agents能不能成为其中的一员，然后是优秀的一员。对于我来说重复发明这些轮子的原因或许是给那些认同这些理念的人留在开源Agent的一个理由，又或者是试着让开发保持社区性的理由（其实不少公司运营的开源项目已经开始拒绝贡献，而且在不少性能重要的领域越来越多人借助越来越强的AI开始进行一次性开发，的确当兼容性被彻底忽视的时候性能优化其实很容易做到极致）。在这个版本的更新中有一个非常重要的推进是提供了第一次相对完整的性能实测和横向对比（docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/，Windows 11 x86_64、i7-14650HX、32 GiB、NVMe机器上的初步观察；如果展示能用Latex或者HTML就更好了，但这也是吹毛求疵，这项工作非常值得赞扬）。从实测来看，sprawling在 1到40个会话时，空闲和活跃状态下的私有内存都稳定在个位数到十几 MiB的量级，而对比的其他harness动辄几十到上千MiB。之前几版我反复强调内存是规模化的真正瓶颈——当你真正跑起多居民、多建筑、长时间工作的城市时，内存会先于 CPU 把你拖垮。这次的数字至少证明了我们在这条路上没有走偏，一定程度上来说优化内存表现就像优化F1赛车，的确1%的提升就算没有比起普通赛车也很快了，但在真正的F1赛场上（比如说上千Agent实际业务场景，想想这些内存优势和硬盘优势会为你节省多少钱）即使是这点优势也会很大程度上影响名次。我希望每个月都有一个版本专门用于调试优化性能，并在下一个版本时更新性能Benchmark实测。

本版实际落地的核心变更主要有两块：一是Console/TUI的大幅推进，CLI现在作为transcript和live region，由Zig leaf绘制，终端里的体验已经相对可用，尤其适合开发板或低资源场景；二是第一次相对完整的性能实测与横向对比，结果记录在docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/，覆盖了启动延迟、文件工具周期、会话内存、固定任务完成率等，并与codex、hermes、pi、deepseek-harness在同一台Windows 11机器上做了对比。详细数字、局限说明和原始csv/manifest都在那里，docs/performance.md也更新了入口。其余还有输入settled处理、delegated child启动失败上报、确认码速率限制、building egress列表、CI按变更重建、Issue标签体系、AGENTS.md工作流调整等，具体可看对应PR。值得讨论的还有很多，之后每周五的ReleaseNote某种意义上会成为博客，当然当贡献者多出来我会尽可能确保不参杂太多大家不喜欢的东西，优先考虑贡献者的感受，确保项目的开放/透明性。我不会再继续ReleaseNote里面罗列ToDo，而是更透明地直接发成Issue，如果你对这个功能感兴趣直接基于Issue提交PR即可。鉴于我不再全身心投入项目高强度开发，我没办法给出相对完整的未来路线图，目前只能期望年内发布v0.1.0beta（其实我对于beta的定义约等于一些项目对v1.0.0的定义，而且我对项目的要求比不少项目还高，但我真正想展示的是诚实地公布各种信息，因为sprawling agents不是商业项目，它没有虚伪或竞争过XX乃至宣发这些的需求，我个人反而不希望在Beta前把它推荐给那些没接触过Agent也不会在Github上发Issue反馈的用户，这不负责），不过倒没有很大问题，我不靠这个项目赚钱或获得工作，能保持自己认为的标准反而更重要，避开versionmaxxing（其实现在项目有一些commitmaxxing的情况，目前定位是AGENTS.md里面的工作流设计有点问题，考虑到也没人真的去看commit记录我就不管了，不过提醒一下贡献者，800新增的规则实际上没有真实的门禁，我只是不想Agent一开始就为了修复1个bug把两三个模块重写了。如果你真的在处理一个很大的问题而超过了800行，请不要拆分pr，会让审核变得困难），鉴于目前开发从个人推Commit转向PR，的确没什么必要写Changinglog，因而粒度可能没有那么细致。

期待您以各种形式参与到项目中。

**In English / 英文版**

Welcome to sprawling v0.0.12 Alpha 261017 (DAYBREAK)!
The signing through SignPath I promised for this version has not come through yet; perhaps it needs a little longer, and a little longer again. For personal reasons — energy and resources are the core of it, but not the whole of it — I will put less into sprawling agent development from this version on. I will not drive features and fixes with a frantic stream of commits as I did before, though that does not mean going fully lazy either. I was never a professional developer, and sprawling agent is my first big project; I started it only because it looked like it might be fairly simple (remember that sprawling agents began as a dull, pure-Rust weekend project and stayed unusable through more than a month of Pre-Alpha), and the pace of development has since told me that it is not simple at all. If you want to take part, or even become a collaborator, send a contribution or write to me (the address is on my GitHub profile). In six months to a year, if this project still has readers, I will put energy and resources into it again (if I still have them by then). For a long time from now I will be responsible only for three things. 1. Filing feature issues. 2. Reviewing issues: if you would rather not implement an issue as a PR, any contributor with the energy and resources is welcome — a first contribution most of all — to turn one of my issues, or an issue I recommend converting, into a PR (if this is your first contribution, the issues I have opened are the best place to start, above all bug fixes, documentation and repository housekeeping: those have clear boundaries and controlled changes, and are the quickest to review and merge; for a large feature, open an issue and explain it before you start). I will help as far as my ability reaches. 3. On Fridays — it could be any day, but one release every two weeks at the slowest and two a week at the fastest seems the right pace, Friday for now, adjustable to any Friday from UTC-12 to UTC+14, and today every release still lands on the same day across East Asia — I will publish a new Release whenever Main has moved since last week's tag.

Strictly speaking, now is a time when far more open-source Agents are needed. I have never thought that there are already enough Agent projects, let alone that developing an Agent is some kind of vibe-coding hello world (writing hello world does not cost money). In the Bot era we saw Muse/Grok Bot in the United States and Qwen/Workbuddy in China begin to gain users in large numbers, even though their models had not become SOTA in their own countries. In the past, only companies chasing SOTA were willing to let you plug in an Agent with a subsidised subscription — Anthropic, for example; OpenAI is now funnelling most of its allowance into Dot, though even without the resets OpenAI used to be the lab with the highest subscription subsidy. They believed that people who used their models more would come to depend deeply on SOTA models and become more important figures in the industry, which would matter enormously to a company's valuation or its ability to win enterprise customers. This 2C is in essence a roundabout 2B, especially when most of an AI company's spending is carried by investment and the core of its revenue comes from the top 10–20% of spenders. From XXClaw to XXWork to XXBot, big companies keep advancing a deeper grip on personal information and consumption, as I warned in an earlier Release Note; reality may well be worse. AI costs are so high that a subscription is in fact the vendor losing money to lock users in. To put it conservatively: for a leading lab, if push advertising were banned, if data went to training, and if no competitor strong enough to take the market existed, cracking down hard on users would actually help save compute and cut costs (hint: which means you have to read that sentence backwards). But strictly speaking, what kind of Personal Agent do we actually need? I think the direction sprawling agent is taking now is the more correct approach, and Agents mired in the "digital maid" or "Jarvis" illusion plainly overestimate what models can do — here I mean the single-Agent designs that make an Agent more entertaining, SOUL.md, memory systems, Persona.md…: at their kindest, a sweet death; at their harshest, a torment. A separate workspace plus a pile of Markdown plus MCP is all you need. If that is not enough, polish computer use and phone (Android) use (the interesting part is that Doubao Phone ran into resistance from a great many vendors, but most of those vendors have not resisted the phone's accessibility mode, so for an open-source Agent there is really no obstacle). If AI's development only brings better push notifications inside shopping apps — from a hand-written algorithm to a small model, say — then AI has not made our world better; it has to change our lives rather than pour fuel on the parts of them that are already bad. Imagine this: you are a university student who wants fully automated course-farming, online exams, food delivery and an electronic girlfriend; how do you solve it? Write one giant Markdown (or, more cleverly, a pile of SKILLs), or keep listing your requirements and have them vectorised, stored and recalled on demand? If you deploy the Agent on a cloud computer, storage becomes the first bottleneck, then running memory, and worst of all degraded output and crossed flavours — especially since most people keep a personal Agent on a Flash model, while a less intelligent model needs deeper optimisation rather than less; perhaps the IKEA effect explains some people's fervour, because I have hardly ever seen a Flash-model user run an ablation experiment. What you should do is divide separate workspaces and give them the SKILLs and tools they need, which keeps the context clean and saves some cost too: let the Agent farm courses and take exams in a real browser on pages where I am logged in (computer use); order food for me in an emulator through accessibility and a stacked-exam or personal-taste SKILL (phone use); and finally, in a sandbox, let an Agent that speaks the Onebot protocol rather than the official one chat with me directly in a social app and write my preferences into the matching workspace's AGENTS.md (proactive ability plus multi-platform access). I will not let the Agent farming my courses know what dishes I like, nor does it need to know why I was unhappy yesterday; it only has to tap the screen now and then, and when it sees a question, search for the answer and reply… In the end, I do not accept that a centralised butler is the right management scheme. A Personal Agent should be a kind of decentralised swarm of Agents, with a Harness providing the integrated scheme — and integrated does not mean a single Harness on your computer: for example, using ACP to drive Claude Code on the machine with Claude and Codex CLI with GPT, while genuinely sensitive content is handled by a small model, staying the whole time inside a WebUI I designed myself and letting each model work in the environment it likes best; in my view there should not be only one Harness on anyone's computer — recently some humorous closed-source Harnesses will help users deploy a suitable open local model for their machine's performance, and of course I am not worried at all about local inference leaking. But the discussion of what the best Personal Agent is is nowhere near over; the community should be talking about it far more, instead of letting the big companies define it. If I had a Coding Agent in the future, I would want its Harness open-source, its context transparent, its model access to include a locally deployed small model or a ZDR-capable model together with SOTA models, its data stored in a fixed local path in a form I can conveniently inspect, edit and delete, and its most sensitive information encrypted at rest. It is true that open-source configuration is a kind of "friction" in the experience compared with a big company's out-of-the-box scheme, but friction is not necessarily bad: to a degree, configuring an open-source Agent is itself learning how it works and practising how to tune it. Many people who use several open-source Agents at once end up building one of their own, and they do not uninstall their own Agent once it is finished; they keep using several, so there is a community of Agent developers in a sense. Those who use an out-of-the-box scheme, by contrast, are usually satisfied with the convenience at first and later, when they want to go deeper, find that they cannot dig down through the convenience they already have. About 10–15 years ago, many people discussed getting root on a phone; it is still useful today (to skip ads, for instance), but the difficulty of getting root is not on the same level as it was. Vendors sell us a black box, bundle software, plant ads, and trade privacy among apps; you cannot open the box, but you can trade it in while it still works (and by the way, they usually ask you to restore the factory settings before shipping it back — but if you have read IEEE 2883.1, then for an SSD a quick format does not even reach Clear). Of course, complete data sovereignty is not only technically difficult but extremely expensive, and most people should not pursue it; what most people can consider is paying more attention to the progress of open-source communities, using open-source projects, and using them to reduce their own data leakage and dependence on big companies.

Of course I also have some other directions I am interested in and could try to develop. sprawling agents is itself a harness that pushes runtime performance and storage overhead to the front of the field — if you want to become a maintainer, an obsession with performance optimisation will be a shared topic between us, provided I can keep up with you — so setting the agents part aside, building an Agent that runs on a development board is not complicated. I have added a reasonably usable TUI in this version: a CLI transcript and a live region drawn by a Zig leaf, with the screenshots below. On the screens a development board usually has, ASCII drawing is quite enough as "generative UI"; the more formal generative UI is currently a Svelte-based scheme in an issue. Imagine paying less than a hundred dollars once and getting a cute box with a screen, a microphone, a speaker, and even feet and a camera, running Linux inside; install Ghostty for a beautiful terminal, run sprawling agents on it with access to various models… The market already has many choices in that price range: a complete Raspberry Pi 5 kit sits around that budget, and the RK3588 boards from Orange Pi, Radxa and FriendlyELEC — I found them by casually searching a shopping platform, and I am sorry if none of the products suits you — can also push 4–8 GB of memory down to about a hundred dollars; with a small screen and a case, that becomes a real "Agent box" you can put on a desk. If optimisation reaches that level, then with a slightly higher budget the same is possible on a used laptop at the same price or a little more — what this sentence means is that you can run the Agent on an old device rather than actually buying second-hand — and they already come with a complete set of IO and cooling. Once performance optimisation is in place, these devices are no longer just toys but personal nodes that can genuinely run a multi-resident city. On the other side, a VPS for about 5 to 10 dollars a month is enough to deploy sprawling agents on a trustworthy cloud platform — not a one-stop platform that wires in a few MCPs or stuffs in a few SKILLs for you after deployment — and to open the WebUI to the public internet so you can use it from any device, which is entirely sufficient for a pure personal Agent scenario. The hardware box and the cloud deployment are in fact two sides of one thing for optimisation: one turns the Agent into a physical object on your desk, the other into a remote workspace you can open at any time. If sprawling agents can keep pushing runtime and storage overhead and latency down, both paths will be easier to walk than they are now. Of course, quite a few harnesses can already do the scenarios above; I am just wondering whether sprawling agents can become one of them, and then an outstanding one. For me, the reason to reinvent these wheels is perhaps to give people who share these ideas a reason to stay with an open-source Agent, or to try to keep development communal — in fact quite a few open-source projects run by companies have started refusing contributions, and in many performance-important fields more and more people use ever-stronger AI for one-off development; when compatibility is thoroughly ignored, performance optimisation is indeed easy to push to the extreme. A very important advance in this version is the first relatively complete performance measurement and cross-comparison (docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/, preliminary observations on a Windows 11 x86_64, i7-14650HX, 32 GiB, NVMe machine; it would be even nicer if the presentation used LaTeX or HTML, but that is nitpicking — this work deserves a lot of praise). The measurements show sprawling at 1 to 40 sessions holding private memory in the single-digit to low-teens MiB range, idle and active alike, while the other harnesses compared range from tens to over a thousand MiB. In the last few versions I kept stressing that memory is the real bottleneck of scale: when you actually run a city with many residents, many buildings and long working hours, memory will drag you down before the CPU does. These numbers at least show that we have not gone off course. Optimising memory is in a way like optimising an F1 car: a 1% gain is fast even against an ordinary car, but on a real F1 track — a real business scenario with a thousand Agents, say; think how much money those memory and disk advantages will save you — even that much advantage greatly affects your place. I hope every month has one version devoted to debugging and optimising performance, with the measured benchmark updated in the version after it.

The core changes that actually landed in this version are mainly two. First, a big push on the Console/TUI: the CLI is now a transcript and a live region drawn by a Zig leaf, and the experience in the terminal is reasonably usable, especially on a development board or a low-resource machine. Second, the first relatively complete performance measurement and cross-comparison, recorded under docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/, covering startup latency, the file-tool cycle, session memory and fixed-task completion rates, and compared with codex, hermes, pi and deepseek-harness on the same Windows 11 machine. The detailed numbers, the statement of limits and the raw csv/manifest are all there, and docs/performance.md has the updated entry point. The rest includes settled-input handling, reporting a delegated child that fails to start, the confirmation-code rate limit, the building egress list, CI rebuilding only what a change reached, the issue label system, the AGENTS.md workflow adjustments and so on; see the corresponding PRs. There is a great deal more worth discussing. The weekly Friday Release Note will in a sense become a blog; when contributors grow in number I will do as much as I can to keep out things most people dislike and to put contributors' feelings first, and to keep the project open and transparent. I will no longer list ToDos in the Release Note, but publish them directly as issues, which is more transparent: if a feature interests you, submit a PR against the issue. Since I am no longer putting my whole self into high-intensity development, I cannot give a relatively complete future roadmap; for now I can only hope to publish v0.1.0 beta within the year — my definition of beta is roughly what some projects call v1.0.0, and my standards for the project are higher than many projects', but what I really want to show is honest disclosure of all kinds of information, because sprawling agents is not a commercial project, it has no need for hypocrisy or for competing with XX or for marketing, and personally I would rather not recommend it before Beta to users who have never touched an Agent and would not file an issue on GitHub to give feedback, which would be irresponsible. Still, that is not a big problem: I do not make money or get a job from this project, and keeping the standards I believe in matters more. I avoid versionmaxxing — in fact the project has some commitmaxxing now; the current position is that the workflow design in AGENTS.md has some problems, and since nobody really reads the commit history I leave it alone, but a reminder to contributors: the 800-added-line rule is not really a gate; I simply do not want an Agent to rewrite two or three modules at the start just to fix one bug. If you are really dealing with a very large problem and go past 800 lines, please do not split the PR, because that makes review harder. Given that development has moved from me pushing commits to PRs, there is indeed little need to write a Changelog, so the granularity may not be that fine.

I look forward to your participation in the project, in any form.

---

**Notes / 补充**

- **The console / 控制台** — The terminal is now a console worth reading. The CLI draws two parts: a transcript written once into the terminal's own scrollback (the banner, what was said, each run's head, its calls, its reply and its ending), and a live region redrawn on each frame (what waits, who works, the calls under way, the quit question, and a composer laid out like the WebUI's). Both are drawn by the new `sprawling-console-ffi` package through a Zig leaf behind one safe function; a control character in a model's reply is drawn as U+FFFD instead of reaching the terminal as a command, Tab opens a menu over the slash verbs and Enter takes the one under the cursor, and the time gutter reads the zone of the machine the city runs on. The quiet host and `/quit` are as 0.0.11 left them. Screenshots: [a session](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/images/console-a-session.png), [the quiet host](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/images/console-quiet-host.png), [the slash menu](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/images/console-slash-menu.png) and [waiting, in a light theme](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/images/console-waiting-light.png); [the guide](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#the-box-the-commands-and-the-keyboard) describes them. Because the renderer is a Zig leaf compiled into every binary, `cargo install sprawling` now needs Zig 0.17.0 on PATH on Linux and macOS as well as Windows; the prebuilt channels need nothing extra.

  终端现在是一个值得看的控制台。CLI 画两部分：一份只写一次、进入终端自身回滚缓冲区的 transcript（banner、说过的话、每个 run 的开头、它的调用、答复和结局），以及每帧重画的 live region（谁在等、谁在工作、进行中的调用、退出提问，以及一个与 WebUI 同布局的输入区）。两者都由新的 `sprawling-console-ffi` 包经 Zig leaf 绘制，叶后面只有一个安全函数；模型答复里的控制字符画成 U+FFFD，而不是作为命令送进终端；Tab 在斜杠动词上打开菜单，Enter 取光标下的那一个；时间栏读城市所在机器的时区。安静宿主和 `/quit` 与 0.0.11 相同。截图：一次会话、安静宿主、斜杠菜单和浅色主题下的等待；入门指南有说明。因为渲染器是编进每个二进制的 Zig leaf，`cargo install sprawling` 现在在 Linux 和 macOS 上同样需要 PATH 里有 Zig 0.17.0；预构建渠道不需要额外的东西。

- **Performance measurements / 性能实测** — [docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/tree/main/docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11) records the first fixed-version measurements, on one Windows 11 x86_64 machine (i7-14650HX, 32 GiB, NVMe): startup and first-answer latency, fixed file tools, session memory, live six-case tasks and a 12-case coding extension, against codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, Hermes Agent v0.21.6+767.g745380d, pi 0.84.4 and deepseek-harness 0.2.0-rc.2. Private memory from 1 to 40 sessions is 6.66 to 11.32 MiB idle and 9.77 to 118.14 MiB active-waiting, the active total counting the city's service and its CLI clients; the other harnesses read from tens to more than three thousand MiB. `python verify.py` recalculates the exported samples without a provider or a credential, and the manifest names the conditions, the accounting and every incomplete cell. These are observations of fixed versions on one machine, not a cross-device ranking, and the performance register in [docs/performance.md](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/performance.md) is unchanged.

  第一次固定版本实测已经记录在 docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/，全部在一台 Windows 11 x86_64 机器上完成（i7-14650HX、32 GiB、NVMe）：启动与首个答复延迟、固定文件工具、会话内存、六个实测任务和 12 个编码扩展任务，对照 codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2、Hermes Agent v0.21.6+767.g745380d、pi 0.84.4 和 deepseek-harness 0.2.0-rc.2。1 到 40 个会话时，sprawling 的空闲私有内存是 6.66 到 11.32 MiB，活跃等待时是 9.77 到 118.14 MiB（活跃总量计入了城市服务与它的 CLI 客户端）；对照的其他 harness 从几十 MiB 到三千多 MiB。`python verify.py` 不需要 provider 或凭证就能重算导出的样本，manifest 写明了条件、统计口径和每一个未完成的格子。这些是固定版本在一台机器上的观察，不是跨设备排名，docs/performance.md 里的性能基线没有改变。

- **Keep-warm / 保温** — A five-minute keep-warm now sends one renewal after a real use, a fixed margin before the cache's lifetime ends, and the renewal runs off the accounting thread, so a silent provider no longer holds up relays and commands. The lead it plans by is measured per endpoint, from sending to the provider starting the request. Settings says "renew once after use" instead of promising a renewal every five minutes, and a room's own `[cache] keep_warm` wins over its building's and the city's, because that is where the dispatch reads it. A renewal is billed: its spend joins the cost total and the room's row, the other four cuts take it in a `keep_warm` bucket, a renewal no provider priced counts as an unpriced call, and the cost page draws the spend as its own line inside the total, with how many renewals were sent and how many came too late to read the cache.

  五分钟保温现在只在一次真实使用之后发一次续期，时点定在缓存寿命结束前一个固定余量，续期跑在记账线程之外，所以沉默的 provider 不再挡住 relay 和命令。它据以规划的提前量按端点测量，量的是从发出到 provider 开始处理这一次请求。设置页写的是「用后续期一次」，不再承诺每五分钟续期一次；房间自己的 `[cache] keep_warm` 胜过它所在的楼和城市，因为派活就在房间这一层读它。续期计入账单：它的花费进入成本总额和房间那一行，其余四张切分表把它记进 `keep_warm` 桶，provider 没有定价的续期算作未定价调用；成本页在总额之内单列这笔花费，并显示发出多少次续期、多少次太晚而没读到缓存。

- **Pre-warm / 预热** — The followers of a cold wave wait behind one pre-warm of the shared prefix, so the wave pays one cache write instead of one per follower; a call the endpoint refuses locally is never pre-warmed, and a confidential building's request is never held, because its pre-warm would carry exactly the bytes that building keeps on this machine. A delegated child opens on the provider account its mother's room is bound to, so it shares her cache. A call that waited at the gate writes a `prefix_held` line.

  冷启动并发里的后来者会等在共享前缀的一次预热后面，于是这一波只付一次缓存写入，而不是每个后来者各付一次；端点会在本地拒绝的调用从不预热，机密楼里的请求也从不被拦住，因为它的预热恰好带着那栋楼留在城市里的字节。被委派的子节点在母亲房间绑定的 provider 账户上开始，因此共享她的缓存。在门前等待过的调用会写一条 `prefix_held` 行。

- **Attach, and the model table / 接入与模型表** — Attaching no longer rewrites what you typed: the form shows one line, "the city calls <recorded>", and leaves the box and the face alone. The model table asks the city what it would register under each empty box and draws that figure as the placeholder with the rung that stated it — the person, the provider's list, an earlier registration, the catalog or a preset, then the policy default — from one ladder in `gateway::provider::ceiling`; a window no rung states reads "unknown", and an unstated ceiling on the chat and responses faces reads "the provider's default". A model id typed into its own box is registered as a named row on the person's word even when the endpoint's list does not carry it, and the table marks it "named by you, not listed by the endpoint". A re-attach whose list cannot be read keeps the rows already registered. An attach is refused, with its code, its subject and the way out drawn under the model table, when a ticked list matches nothing served, or when the rows it would register drop a model a role points at. On the wire, `AttachEndpoint` carries the typed ids apart from the ticked ones and each row says whether it was listed or named.

  接入不再改写你输入的东西：表单只显示一行「the city calls \<recorded\>」，不动输入框和接口形态。模型表会问城市：每个空框会登记成什么，把那个数字画成占位符，并标出是哪一级说的——人、provider 列表、更早的登记、目录或预设、策略默认——它们都在 `gateway::provider::ceiling` 的同一把梯子上；没有一级声明的窗口读作「unknown」，chat 和 responses 面上未声明的上限读作「the provider's default」。在你自己的输入框里手填的模型 id，即使端点列表里没有，也按你的话登记为 named 行，表格会标上「named by you, not listed by the endpoint」。列表读不回来的重新接入，保留已经登记的行。勾选的列表一个已服务的模型都没匹配上、或者这次登记会丢掉某个角色正指向的模型时，接入被拒绝，代码、主体和出路画在模型表下面。协议上，`AttachEndpoint` 把 typed id 与勾选行分开携带，每一行都写明它是 listed 还是 named。

- **Smaller changes / 其余小改动** — A key an input method is composing with now passes through in the combobox, the palette, the file finder, the workspace pill and the two Escape fields, and a branch moves main only after the city has opened the branch. A delegated child the hand-over refuses goes back to its parent's room as a stopped handback carrying the refusal's code, subject and recovery, so a parent learns that the child never started. The console confirmation for a remote door reads one answer a second and locks after ten judged misses, closing the door at that moment. A building's egress list now holds both the city's browser and the person's: a building that wrote no list keeps every host, an empty list reaches no public host, a confidential building is the empty list, and a host is read with the WHATWG parser a browser follows. Issues carry the label system from `.github/labels.yml` — type, area, aspect and status — and the contribution guide's *Other projects* section says when a contribution may name another project.

  输入法正在组合的按键现在在 combobox、命令面板、文件查找、工作区胶囊和两个 Escape 输入框里都会放行；分支只有在城市真正打开分支之后才移动 main。转交阶段拒绝的委派子节点会作为 stopped handback 回到父亲房间，带着那次拒绝的 code、subject 和 recovery，父亲因此知道孩子从未启动。远端门的控制台确认每秒只读一个答案，十次读到的失败之后上锁，并在那一刻关闭已打开的远端门。楼的 egress 列表现在同时约束城市浏览器和人的浏览器：没有写列表的楼保留所有主机，空列表到不了任何公网主机，机密楼等于空列表；主机按浏览器遵循的 WHATWG 解析器读取。Issue 采用四轴标签——type、area、aspect 和 status——贡献指南规定了贡献什么时候可以提到另一个项目。

- **CI and toolchain / CI 与工具链** — CI rebuilds only what a change reached: the test build takes the client bundle from a cache keyed by `client/` and starts from the target directory main left, replaced cache entries and closed pull requests' entries are pruned, render passes open in parallel and the swap test has a runner of its own, eslint runs on every core, the Zig leaves rebuild on a source or pin change rather than a PATH change, and the dev profile writes no debug information. The `docnum` gate no longer holds the test count, `length` no longer caps a file, and `modmap` no longer needs a row for a test module. The ACP v1 schema is re-read at the upstream commit the adapter is built against, and the advisories RustSec published on 2026-10-16 are cleared before this release: `rustls` 0.23.46 and `wasmtime` 48.0.6 replace versions the database flags, and `zip` 9.0.4 replaces the yanked 8.6.0.

  CI 只重建一次变更真正触及的东西：测试构建从以 `client/` 为键的缓存取客户端 bundle，并从 main 留下的 target 目录起步；被替换的缓存条子和已关闭 PR 的条子会被清掉；render 检查并行打开多轮，swap 测试有自己的 runner；eslint 用上所有核心；两个 Zig leaf 在源文件或 pin 变化时重建，而不是 PATH 变化时；dev profile 不写调试信息。`docnum` 不再把测试数量当事实，`length` 不再限制文件长度，`modmap` 不再要求测试模块登记。ACP v1 schema 按适配器所依据的上游 commit 重新读过；RustSec 在 2026-10-16 发布的公告在本版发布前已清掉：`rustls` 升到 0.23.46、`wasmtime` 升到 48.0.6，被 yank 的 `zip` 8.6.0 换成 9.0.4。

- **Backward compatibility / 向后兼容** — The Ledger's event-log version is still 2, and a line written by 0.0.11 reads back unchanged; 0.0.12 adds the `prefix_held` kind and folds `cache_renewed` lines differently. The wire moved from WIRE_V 65 to 67 — a new query name moves the schema hash on its own, and two frames changed shape — so a browser tab from 0.0.11 is refused rather than misread; reload it against the new city. A views or standing snapshot cut by 0.0.11 is refused by version and folded again from the start of the Ledger, because the fold rules changed, and the console says so. Nothing has to be converted by hand. A city that asked for keep-warm under 0.0.11 still does; a building that wrote `browser = true` beside `egress = []` now reaches no public host, which is what its file says; the blank form a new building is laid out with no longer writes that pair.

  账本格式版本仍是 2，0.0.11 写下的行照原义读回；0.0.12 新增 `prefix_held` 这一 kind，并按新的规则折叠 `cache_renewed` 行。协议从 WIRE_V 65 升到 67——新查询名本身就会推动 schema hash，另有两处帧改了形状——所以 0.0.11 的浏览器标签页会被明确拒绝而不是读错，对新城市重新加载即可。0.0.11 切下的视图或常驻状态快照按版本被拒绝，再从头折叠账本，因为折叠规则变了，控制台会说明这一点。不需要手工转换任何东西。0.0.11 里要求保温的城市照旧保温；写了 `browser = true` 又写了 `egress = []` 的楼现在到不了任何公网主机，这正是它文件里写的；新楼铺设用的空白表单不再写下这一对。

- **Known limits / 已知限制** — The Windows binary is still unsigned, so Windows Defender may quarantine a downloaded archive. A process running as your account, which includes an ACP agent you added, can read the key file and drive the city. A crash can leave child processes running; "Stop now" ends a run at its next safe point but does not cancel a model call already in flight. An upstream that refuses a thinking level it stated is asked for it again. The renewal counts on the cost page are city-wide, because the cost view has no per-room page. The published measurements keep their unattempted cells and incomplete usage exactly as the [benchmark README](https://github.com/2youg1/sprawling-agents/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v0.0.11/README.md) records them.

  Windows 二进制仍未签名，Windows Defender 可能隔离下载的归档。以你的账户运行的进程，包括你添加的 ACP agent，能读到密钥文件并操作城市。崩溃后子进程可能还在运行；「立刻停下」会在下一个安全点结束 run，但不会取消已经发出的模型调用。上游拒绝了它自己声明过的思考档位，下一次仍会再问一次。成本页上的续期计数是全城范围的，因为成本视图没有按房间的页面。已公布的实测保留未完成的格子和不完整的用量，与实测说明记录的一致。

**What comes next** — the author's plan for the near term, written where a roadmap would go: a Release every Friday while Main has moved since the last tag, with one version each month devoted to performance work and the measurement updated in the version after it; new ToDos published as issues rather than listed here, which is where a contribution starts; Windows code signing through SignPath once the Foundation issues the certificate; and the exploration of generative UI, beginning with interactive widgets generated from the conversation. No version or date is promised for `v0.1.0` Beta, and finishing any item here does not by itself make it.
